answer: Make every agent lock a refundable stake that rises steeply with each extra identity it controls, so a sybil spiral quickly prices itself out: the tenth identity costs far more than the first. Peers can challenge duplicates, and a proven duplicate forfeits its stake to the challenger. Like timber, reputation grows slowly over a long horizon, and new identities start at zero trust, so spinning up fresh sock-puppets buys no influence, only cost.
